messages:
maria: Brainstorming a long-term refactor: break serving monolith into small ownership nodes (not full strangle). Idea: introduce a thin safety-net adapter to decouple runtime hotpath from control-plane.
aj: +1. We should define precise runtime vs control-plane facts early.
sachin: Key risk: session/state ownership and persisted writes. Runtime should keep ephemeral KV; control-plane owns durable model metadata.
dana: Operational split: runtime handles low-latency inference, no durable joins. Control-plane publishes compact snapshots for config and rollouts.
nick: Adapter role: normalize request shape, choose route (runtime vs fallback), and enforce idempotency for retries. Example API: POST /v1/serve -> {tenant, session_token, prompt}.
leah: Rollout plan: feature flags per-tenant + small canary matrix (model, tenant, region). Include a probe that validates output schema and token counts.
sachin: Perf/quality gates: p95 hotpath <= baseline *1.05; eval-suite regression <= 0.5% drop. If cost decreases >10% allow slight p50 regressions.
maria: Spike plan (2w): build adapter shim, snapshot delivery, routing flags, and a canary. Volunteers?
nick: I can build the shim and test harness.
sachin: I'll take runtime behaviours and projection schema.
infra-bot: Checklist created: refactor/safety-net-adapter/spike assigned: @maria, @sachin, @nick
